classing_rule: FILE_DAY: the day comes from the object key, or the object for day D is loaded and every row in it is treated as day D. TRANSACTION_DATE: rows are placed by a date column of the row; a key date that only bounds a cache with a full-rebuild fallback on any changed object, or only breaks ties between duplicate ids, does not place a row and is stated in the basis. BOTH: the key date decides which objects' rows enter the output (no such fallback) AND the row date places them, or the code reads both and says so. NEITHER: reads every object, uses no day.

schema.read_from: the footer of the oldest version of each of the two day objects (74 columns; date columns by name or by timestamp/date type)
schema.columns_projected_in_the_read: transaction_id plus the 13 date columns above; no money column, no account column

days.date_column_used: trade_date (the transaction's own trade date; the date column the row-date readers group on). An id counts when every one of its rows carries that date.
trade_date (the transaction's own trade date; the date column the row-date readers group on). An id counts when every one of its rows carries that date.

answer.basis: 10 of 32 readers are classed FILE_DAY or BOTH (3 FILE_DAY, 7 BOTH): 8 on the served side and 2 on the tie-out side. The 2 on the tie-out side are the two diagnostics that record the copy's partition name beside the row's return_date (b2_read.py, b3_loc.py); no tie-out figure is placed by the partition, the other 13 tie-out producers key on the row's own return_date or read every object.
answer.what_it_means: For the two days, 5580 ids (4545 + 1035, every id the two day files held then) sit now in a file of a different day (the files two days earlier), and none sits in the old day's file. A reader that places an id by its file's day (B_03.account_gains.py line 327; bd_price_update.py line 265 and its lambda twin line 143) would place all 5580 on a different day than before. At the object's own dates the ids never matched the old file day (trade_date and return_date equal to the old file day for 0 ids then) and match the new file day for return_date on every id and for trade_date on 4505 + 1030. No served figure is recomputed here.
answer.row_date_readers: Readers that place by trade_date or return_date are unaffected in placement by the move: each id's own date values are unchanged from the old version to the current objects (every one of the 5580 ids, for every date column but the ingest stamp as_of_date).
